title: Arriving in Berlin: rehearsal bedlam and hotel costs
summary: He praises Berlin's cleanliness, describes Lyons, Germans and Russians shouting in different languages, and the expensive Prager Platz hotel.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: So, anyway, you got to Europe and you went straight to Berlin. Is that right?

Yep. Well, Berlin was alright. Berlin was the most beautiful city I'd ever seen. The streets were perfect. They were clean. And one thing that we enjoyed was that all the houses in the block were painted -- if they were all blue, they were all blue, if they were all green, it was all green. And this was a new aspect in our life completely, you see.
And we took the best of it. We used to go down to the Lust Gardens, and to the Unter den Linden. And we'd go to Tier Park and --
But tell me, where did you -- did you have to rehearse, then, before you actually went on in Berlin?

I don't know how Arthur Lyons got that show on. For the simple reason that they had -- most of the stagehands were Russian. Germans were there and the Russians and English. Now, it was more of a bedlam. It was more bedlam because the Russians -- and that's when I knew and Arthur asked me -- and he was talking Russian. And then he couldn't speak German, but we had a Jewish fellow with us named Goldberg. Goldberg spoke Yiddish. So Yiddish and German were the same, and he was talking Yiddish, Arthur Lyons was talking Russian, and the Germans were answering back in German and Yiddish and Russian.
And none of you understood any of it.
Where did they put you up. Were you in a hotel?

We were in a hotel called the PRAGER Platz. And that's where we all rebelled on that, and after that we went about our business. Because they wanted to charge us 50 Marks a night, and stuff like that. Well 50 Marks was $12.50 and that was a whole lot of money in those days, see.
But the boys got good money for playing.
And you had to pay for that yourself.
Oh yeah, that's the only thing we had to

And food. We had to pay for food, but the hauling, the trunks and everything like that. All you had to do was to close your wardrobe trunk like that and the man come and get it and move on to the next place.
